minor_characters.name: Bulkington
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly glimpsed as a stoic sailor at the Spouter-Inn (Ch 006) and memorialized in the stand‑alone meditation 'The Lee Shore' (Ch 026)
minor_characters.reason_removable: He has no effect on the Pequod’s voyage or its outcome and is unmentioned in the core arc; removing him trims a self‑contained aside without touching the plot or central themes.

minor_characters.name: Peter Coffin
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The jocular Spouter‑Inn landlord who spars with Ishmael on arrival in New Bedford (Ch 005–006)
minor_characters.reason_removable: The Spouter‑Inn can function with an unnamed innkeeper; his banter adds color but is not needed to establish Ishmael, Queequeg, or the voyage.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Hussey
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The Try Pots proprietress who serves chowder and fusses over boarding‑house rules (Ch 018)
minor_characters.reason_removable: She is a comic grace note; chowder at the Try Pots can be retained in narration without her specific personality or dialogue.

minor_characters.name: Guernsey-mate of the Rose‑Bud
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Mate of the French whaler Rose‑Bud in the ambergris episode, bickering through an interpreter with Stubb (Ch 094)
minor_characters.reason_removable: Comic foil in a detachable encounter; cutting him and the ship’s vignette does not alter the Pequod’s track or Ahab’s pursuit.

minor_characters.name: Captain Boomer (Samuel Enderby)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Genial English captain missing an arm, who warns Ahab off Moby Dick during their gam (Ch 101–103)
minor_characters.reason_removable: His role duplicates warnings Ahab already ignores; the core gams named in the synopsis (Jeroboam, Jungfrau, Rachel) carry the needed braid of rumor and omen.

minor_characters.name: Dr. Bunger
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Wry surgeon aboard the Samuel Enderby who spars verbally with Ahab (Ch 103)
minor_characters.reason_removable: A side comic presence in a removable gam; eliminating him tightens focus on Ahab’s obsession without loss.

minor_characters.name: Captain of the Albatross (Goney)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Silent, unlucky captain of the passing ship Albatross that drops his speaking‑trumpet (Ch 052)
minor_characters.reason_removable: A brief atmospheric omen; the synopsis already preserves the essential gams, so this extra sighting can go without harm.

minor_characters.name: Captain of the Bachelor
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Exultant homeward‑bound master of the Bachelor who invites Ahab aboard (Ch 118)
minor_characters.reason_removable: This celebratory contrast to the Pequod’s doom is dispensable; the Rachel encounter supplies the necessary moral counterpoint late in the arc.

minor_characters.name: The Manxman
minor_characters.appearances_summary: An elderly sailor who mutters fatalistic asides during several deck scenes (e.g., Ch 099–102)
minor_characters.reason_removable: His gnomic color does not affect events or major character arcs; excising him reduces stage‑business without touching the story.

minor_characters.name: Dough‑Boy (steward)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The timid steward who ferries food and gets flustered by mates (e.g., Ch 064, 067, 097)
minor_characters.reason_removable: A bit player for comic texture; removing his lines leaves all whaling action and Ahab’s arc intact.

minor_characters.name: The Manxman (old Manx sailor)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Ch 128–131: chats at the log and line, mutters superstitions about omens and the Rachel, offers commentary during storm work and deaths.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is a color character whose superstitions and quips can be omitted or reassigned to unnamed sailors without affecting any plot turn or a principal character’s arc.

minor_characters.name: The Sicilian seaman
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Ch 133: cries out from the mizzen-mast about Ahab’s hat as a sea-hawk snatches it.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His one-line omen trigger adds atmosphere only, and cutting him (and the hat incident) does not alter events or themes already reinforced elsewhere.

minor_characters.name: The Tahitian (seaman)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Ch 128: helps Ahab heave the log with the Manxman and is briefly addressed in the melee with Pip.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He serves a purely functional role that can be performed by an unnamed hand without changing any outcome or relationship.

minor_characters.name: Captain of the Delight
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Ch 134: the hollow-cheeked master who gams with the Pequod while burying a sailor lost to Moby Dick.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is confined to a single, parallel-incident gam that duplicates omens and losses shown elsewhere and is not required by the synopsis.

subplots.name: The Town‑Ho’s Story
subplots.reason_removable: A long inset tale told off the Pequod that does not change Ahab’s hunt, Ishmael’s arc, or the ship’s fate; cutting it preserves narrative drive.

subplots.name: Bulkington and The Lee Shore
subplots.reason_removable: A lyric memorial to a peripheral sailor; its meditation on freedom and fate duplicates broader themes without affecting the Pequod’s story.

subplots.name: The Rose‑Bud (ambergris trick)
subplots.reason_removable: A comic interlude with a French whaler; amusing but extraneous to Ahab’s pursuit and the named gams that matter to the plot.

subplots.name: The Samuel Enderby gam (Captain Boomer)
subplots.reason_removable: Reiterates warnings Ahab rejects; the Jeroboam and Rachel encounters in the synopsis already supply the braid of rumor, omen, and final moral reckoning.

subplots.name: The Albatross (Goney) sighting
subplots.reason_removable: An atmospheric pass‑by; removing it streamlines the outward passage without weakening the established forebodings.

subplots.name: The Grand Armada nursery‑scene
subplots.reason_removable: A lush set‑piece of whales at play; beautiful but nonessential to the Pequod’s hunt or the climactic pursuit.

subplots.name: The Spirit‑Spout
subplots.reason_removable: A spectral tease that foreshadows Moby Dick; the synopsis already keeps Fedallah’s prophecy and the major gams for fatalism and omen.

subplots.name: The Decanter (Enderby after‑talk)
subplots.reason_removable: A retrospective on the Enderby gam; once that visit is cut, this coda may go as well without loss.

subplots.name: Ahab’s hat carried off by the sea-hawk (the omen of the hat)
subplots.reason_removable: This self-contained omen has no causal effect on the chase or crew and the book’s tapestry of portents is already ample without it.

subplots.name: Gam with the Delight (burial at sea and warning from a ruined crew)
subplots.reason_removable: It is an atmospheric parallel that neither advances the Pequod’s plot nor adds necessities beyond omens already supplied by other gams and scenes.

subplots.name: Starbuck’s midnight temptation with the musket
subplots.reason_removable: Starbuck’s moral caution, piety, and later near-mutiny are fully legible from the typhoon scenes and the third-day plea, so this private crisis can be trimmed without obscuring his arc.

subplots.name: Forecastle nightwork interlude (banter, songs, and brief lashings during the typhoon)
subplots.reason_removable: These short side-scenes provide comic relief and texture but do not change the storm’s outcome, Ahab’s stance, or any later decision.

subplots.name: Orders on deck during the gale (Ahab refuses to strike anything down)
subplots.reason_removable: The same trait—Ahab’s defiant will in storm and omen—is conveyed more forcefully in the St. Elmo’s fire and quadrant/compass chapters.

digressions.topic: Didactic explanation of lightning’s effects on compasses and magnetism at sea.
digressions.reason_removable: Ahab’s forging of a new compass (which the synopsis preserves) carries the dramatic point without the science lesson.

digressions.topic: General essay on the neglect of the log and line among whalemen before the scene itself.
digressions.reason_removable: The needed beats—that the line parts and Ahab later folds Pip to him—survive without the trade-practice preamble.

digressions.topic: Speculations about seal-cries, mermaids, and sailors’ superstitions before the mast-head fall.
digressions.reason_removable: The plot consequence (a lookout falls and the coffin becomes a life-buoy) is intact without the folkloric detour.

digressions.topic: Ahab’s metaphysical riff on the coffin as an ‘immortality-preserver.’
digressions.reason_removable: Its philosophy echoes themes voiced elsewhere, while the practical fact of the coffin’s conversion has already been established.
The chase’s action is self-explanatory on the page and does not require the glossary note.

digressions.topic: Extended analogy on night-and-day pursuit, pilots, compasses, and even railways.
digressions.reason_removable: This essayistic generalization can be lifted without affecting the momentum or clarity of the second day’s chase.
